observation_text: Child was asked to put away toys after playtime.
behavior: Child ignored the request and continued playing with blocks.
consequence: No consequence noted
caregiver_response: Caregiver reminded the child again.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make clean-up more fun?
general_support_idea: Consider setting a timer for transitions.

observation_text: Child was transitioning from outdoor play to snack time.
behavior: Child hesitated and sat down on the ground, not wanting to move.
consequence: Child eventually walked to the snack area after a gentle nudge.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a favorite snack to encourage movement.
suggested_followup_question: What snack would you like next time?
general_support_idea: Try using a signal to indicate transitions.

observation_text: Child was finished with art class and needed to go to lunch.
behavior: Child started to gather supplies but then sat down and began doodling instead.
consequence: Child was reminded about lunch and quickly packed up to join classmates.
caregiver_response: Caregiver encouraged the child by mentioning friends were waiting.
suggested_followup_question: How can we keep the energy up during transitions?
general_support_idea: Discuss using a checklist for transitions.

observation_text: Child was preparing to leave the park after playtime.
behavior: Child refused to leave and started playing tag with friends instead.
consequence: Child joined the group for one last round of tag before leaving.
caregiver_response: Caregiver allowed a short extension on playtime.
suggested_followup_question: What can make leaving a park easier?
general_support_idea: Consider having a 'last game' before transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to leave a friend's house after play.
behavior: Child threw the toy and said they didn’t want to go home.
consequence: Child calmed down after the caregiver suggested a story on the way home.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a story during the car ride.
suggested_followup_question: What story will make the ride home more enjoyable?
general_support_idea: Think about a reward for coming home smoothly.

observation_text: Child struggled to move from one activity to another at daycare.
behavior: Child started crying and clung to a stuffed animal.
consequence: Staff reassured the child with comfort and settled them for nap.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a favorite stuffed toy for comfort.
suggested_followup_question: What soothing techniques work best?
general_support_idea: Explore a visual schedule for transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to stop playing video games for bed.
behavior: Child became upset and raised their voice, refusing to stop playing.
consequence: Child agreed to stop when offered extra time on the weekend.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a compromise with weekend time.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make bedtime smoother?
general_support_idea: Introduce a countdown timer for transitions.

observation_text: Child was asked to leave the grocery store.
behavior: Child wandered down the aisle, ignoring the caregiver's call.
consequence: Child returned to the caregiver after noticing they were leaving the aisle.
caregiver_response: Caregiver explained they needed to go home soon.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can help keep the child close?
general_support_idea: Discuss using a special shopping list together.

observation_text: Child needed to come inside after playing in the yard.
behavior: Child lay on the grass and said they were tired.
consequence: Child eventually got up and walked inside after a few minutes.
caregiver_response: Caregiver suggested a snack indoors would be nice.
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage quicker transitions?
general_support_idea: Consider a fun inside activity after outdoor play.

observation_text: Child was leaving the playground to go to a restaurant.
behavior: Child ran away from the caregiver towards the swings.
consequence: Child was brought back gently and reminded of the plan to eat.
caregiver_response: Caregiver praised the child for listening after they returned.
suggested_followup_question: How can we keep them focused on the next activity?
general_support_idea: Try using visual reminders for the day's schedule.

observation_text: Child was transitioning from lunch to recess at school.
behavior: Child packed slowly, chatting with friends instead of moving out.
consequence: Child finally joined friends outside after a few reminders.
caregiver_response: Caregiver used a timer to signal the end of lunch.
suggested_followup_question: What can keep the excitement for recess?
general_support_idea: Make a fun countdown for transitions.

observation_text: Child needed to stop playing video games to do chores.
behavior: Child shouted that they didn't want to stop.
consequence: Child took a break but complained about it while doing chores.
caregiver_response: Caregiver discussed the importance of responsibilities after gaming.
suggested_followup_question: What chores can we make more fun?
general_support_idea: Create a chore chart with rewards.

observation_text: Child was asked to leave a public restaurant after dinner.
behavior: Child ran towards the door and hesitated to leave.
consequence: Child was reassured and walked out after seeing dessert was next.
caregiver_response: Caregiver mentioned dessert while leaving.
suggested_followup_question: How can we handle leaving a fun place?
general_support_idea: Discuss a small treat for leaving on time.

observation_text: Child was told it was time to transition from playing to bedtime.
behavior: Child threw their blanket and said no to bedtime.
consequence: Child calmed down after the caregiver read a story.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a book to read together.
suggested_followup_question: What story will be the favorite tonight?
general_support_idea: Try a bedtime routine chart.

observation_text: Child was asked to get ready for school.
behavior: Child sat on the floor, fiddling with their backpack.
consequence: Child finally got up and started organizing their things when prompted.
caregiver_response: Caregiver reminded them of the time.
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage getting ready faster?
general_support_idea: Consider a morning checklist together.

observation_text: Child was leaving a relative's house after visiting.
behavior: Child started playing with a toy and ignored the request to leave.
consequence: Child was helped to pack the toy and waved goodbye after reassurance.
caregiver_response: Caregiver suggested a playdate next time.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to make goodbyes easier?
general_support_idea: Discuss planning for the next visit together.

observation_text: Child was asked to leave the playground after a long play.
behavior: Child climbed on the jungle gym and refused to come down.
consequence: Child eventually climbed down after seeing other children leave.
caregiver_response: Caregiver waited patiently at the bottom.
suggested_followup_question: How can we encourage leaving after play?
general_support_idea: Suggest a favorite game to play next time.

observation_text: Child was transitioning from art class to gym class.
behavior: Child started packing slowly and hesitated to move to the next class.
consequence: Child picked up the pace when they heard about a fun activity in gym.
caregiver_response: Caregiver reminded them of the fun that awaited in gym class.
suggested_followup_question: What can encourage a quicker transition?
general_support_idea: Consider sharing what’s exciting in the next class.

observation_text: Child was moving from free play to structured group activity.
behavior: Child began to cry and refused to join the group.
consequence: Child was comforted and settled in with the group after some time.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered support and encouragement.
suggested_followup_question: How can we help with group activities?
general_support_idea: Introduce a familiar face to help ease transitions.

observation_text: Child was supposed to leave the store with the caregiver.
behavior: Child dashed away down the aisle, not paying attention.
consequence: Child was brought back after a few minutes of searching.
caregiver_response: Caregiver looked for the child while calling their name.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can keep them close?
general_support_idea: Consider using a hand-holding agreement while shopping.

observation_text: Child became upset when asked to leave the playground and started crying loudly.
behavior: Child sat down on the ground and refused to move.
consequence: Child eventually got up after a few minutes and walked slowly to the car with caregiver.
caregiver_response: Caregiver offered a countdown to leaving.
suggested_followup_question: What can we do to make transitions easier?
general_support_idea: Using visual timers for transitions can help.

observation_text: Child didn't want to go to a relative's house and hid behind the couch.
behavior: Child clutched a toy tightly and said they wanted to stay home.
consequence: Child relaxed after the caregiver promised to return with a treat later.
caregiver_response: Caregiver suggested bringing a favorite toy along.
suggested_followup_question: How can we make the visit more enjoyable?
general_support_idea: Discussing the fun activities planned can ease anxiety.

observation_text: Child walked away from the caregiver in a store to look at toys without asking permission.
behavior: Child ran toward a display, ignoring the caregiver's call.
consequence: Child returned after being reminded to stay close and help pick a toy.
caregiver_response: Caregiver explained the importance of staying together for safety.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can we use to keep them close while shopping?
general_support_idea: Creating a shopping list together can keep them engaged.

observation_text: Child fussed when it was time to turn off the tablet and move to dinner.
behavior: Child shouted and threw the tablet on the couch.
consequence: Child sat quietly at the table after being reminded of the dinner routine.
caregiver_response: Caregiver set a timer for the next screen time.
suggested_followup_question: How can we create smoother transitions from screen time to other activities?
general_support_idea: Establishing a routine can help with transitions.

observation_text: Child became resistant when asked to leave the playground, running away from caregiver.
behavior: Child sprinted away and climbed a structure.
consequence: Child climbed down after several calls and went to the caregiver cautiously.
caregiver_response: Caregiver calmly explained the need to leave for dinner.
suggested_followup_question: What strategies can I use to help them understand transitions?
general_support_idea: Offering choices during transitions can help them feel in control.
